column1: According to the latest figures, the majority of the world’s population is now bilingual or multilingual, having grown up speaking two or more languages.
column2: 最新数据显示，世界上大多数人如今都会两种或多种语言，他们从小就说至少两种语言。

column1: In the past, such children were considered to be at a disadvantage compared with their monolingual peers.
column2: 过去，人们认为，这样的孩子与只说一种语言的同龄人相比处于劣势。
column3: were considered to be|被认为是
column6: monolingual peers|只说一种语言的同龄人

column1: Over the past few decades, however, technological advances have allowed researchers to look more deeply at how bilingualism interacts with and changes the cognitive and neurological systems, thereby identifying several clear benefits of being bilingual.
column2: 不过，过去几十年的技术进步使研究人员能更深入地探究双语能力如何与认知和神经系统相互作用、引起变化，从而找出了使用双语的若干明显益处。

column1: Research shows that when a bilingual person uses one language, the other is active at the same time.
column2: 研究显示，双语者使用一种语言时，另一种语言也同时处于活跃状态。

column1: When we hear a word, we don’t hear the entire word all at once: the sounds arrive in sequential order.
column2: 听到一个词时，我们并非一下子听到整个词，因为组成它的声音是依次传来的。

column1: Long before the word is finished, the brain’s language system begins to guess what that word might be.
column2: 早在一个词还没说完时，大脑的语言系统就开始推测它可能是什么词。

column1: If you hear ‘can’, you will likely activate words like ‘candy’ and ‘candle’ as well, at least during the earlier stages of word recognition.
column2: 如果听到can这个音，你很可能也会激活candy（糖果）、candle（蜡烛）等词，至少在词汇识别的初期是这样。

column1: For bilingual people, this activation is not limited to a single language; auditory input activates corresponding words regardless of the language to which they belong.
column2: 对双语者而言，这种激活不局限于一种语言。听觉输入会激活与之对应的词，不论它们属于哪一种语言。

column1: Some of the most compelling evidence for this phenomenon, called ‘language co-activation’, comes from studying eye movements.
column2: 研究者把这种现象称为“语言共同激活”。支持它的一些最有说服力的证据，来自对眼球运动的研究。

column1: A Russian-English bilingual asked to ‘pick up a marker’ from a set of objects would look more at a stamp than someone who doesn’t know Russian, because the Russian word for ‘stamp’, marka, sounds like the English word he or she heard, ‘marker’.
column2: 当一个俄英双语者听到指令“拿起一支记号笔（marker）”，需要从一组物品中去取时，他会比不懂俄语的人更多地看向邮票。这是因为俄语中表示“邮票”的marka，与他听到的英语单词marker发音相似。
column4: pick up a marker|拿起一支记号笔
column5: a set of objects|一组物品

column1: In cases like this, language co-activation occurs because what the listener hears could map onto words in either language.
column2: 在这样的情形中，听者听到的声音可以与两种语言中的词相对应，因此会出现语言共同激活。
column3: In cases like this|在这样的情形下
column7: either language|两种语言中的任一种

column1: Having to deal with this persistent linguistic competition can result in difficulties, however.
column2: 不过，不断应付这种语言之间的竞争，也可能带来困难。

column1: For instance, knowing more than one language can cause speakers to name pictures more slowly, and can increase ‘tip-of-the-tongue states’, when you can almost, but not quite, bring a word to mind.
column2: 比如，会多种语言可能使人说出图片中事物名称的速度变慢，也可能让“话到嘴边却说不出”的情况更加常见：差一点就能想起某个词，却总是差那么一点。
column3: name pictures|说出图片中事物的名称
column5: tip-of-the-tongue states|话到嘴边却想不出词的状态
column7: bring a word to mind|想起某个词

column1: As a result, the constant juggling of two languages creates a need to control how much a person accesses a language at any given time.
column2: 因此，不断同时应付两种语言，就要求说话者随时控制自己在多大程度上调用其中一种语言。
column4: creates a need|产生一种需要
column7: at any given time|在任一特定时刻

column1: For this reason, bilingual people often perform better on tasks that require conflict management.
column2: 正因如此，双语者在需要处理冲突的任务上往往表现得更好。

column1: In the classic Stroop Task, people see a word and are asked to name the colour of the word’s font.
column2: 在经典的斯特鲁普任务中，参与者看到一个词，要说出这个词的字体是什么颜色。

column1: When the colour and the word match (i.e., the word ‘red’ printed in red), people correctly name the colour more quickly than when the colour and the word don’t match (i.e., the word ‘red’ printed in blue).
column2: 当颜色和词义一致时，例如“红”字用红色印出，人们能更快地正确说出颜色；当颜色和词义不一致时，例如“红”字用蓝色印出，人们的反应就较慢。
column3: the colour and the word match|颜色与词义相符

column1: This occurs because the word itself (‘red’) and its font colour (blue) conflict.
column2: 这是因为词本身的意思（“红”）与字体颜色（蓝色）相冲突。

column1: Bilingual people often excel at tasks such as this, which tap into the ability to ignore competing perceptual information and focus on the relevant aspects of the input.
column2: 双语者往往特别擅长这类任务，因为任务会用到一种能力，即忽略相互竞争的感知信息，把注意力放在输入信息中与任务有关的部分。
column6: competing perceptual information|相互竞争的感知信息

column1: Bilinguals are also better at switching between two tasks; for example, when bilinguals have to switch from categorizing objects by colour (red or green) to categorizing them by shape (circle or triangle), they do so more quickly than monolingual people, reflecting better cognitive control when having to make rapid changes of strategy.
column2: 双语者也更擅长在两项任务之间切换。例如，在先按颜色（红或绿）给物体分类、再改按形状（圆或三角形）分类时，双语者的切换速度比单语者快。这反映出，需要迅速改变策略时，他们的认知控制能力更好。

column1: It also seems that the neurological roots of the bilingual advantage extend to brain areas more traditionally associated with sensory processing.
column2: 双语优势的神经基础似乎还延伸到了那些传统上更多被认为与感觉处理有关的脑区。

column1: When monolingual and bilingual adolescents listen to simple speech sounds without any intervening background noise, they show highly similar brain stem responses.
column2: 单语和双语青少年在没有任何背景噪声干扰的情况下听简单的语音时，两组的脑干反应高度相似。

column1: When researchers play the same sound to both groups in the presence of background noise, however, the bilingual listeners’ neural response is considerably larger, reflecting better encoding of the sound’s fundamental frequency, a feature of sound closely related to pitch perception.
column2: 不过，研究者在有背景噪声的情况下向两组播放同样的声音时，双语听者的神经反应显著更强。这表明他们能更好地对声音的基频进行编码，而基频是与音高知觉密切相关的一项声音特征。
column3: in the presence of|在有……的情况下

column1: Such improvements in cognitive and sensory processing may help a bilingual person to process information in the environment, and help explain why bilingual adults acquire a third language better than monolingual adults master a second language.
column2: 双语者在认知和感觉处理方面的这些改善，可能有助于他们处理环境中的信息，也有助于解释，为什么成年双语者学习第三种语言，比成年单语者学习第二种语言的效果更好。
column3: cognitive and sensory processing|认知和感觉处理

column1: This advantage may be rooted in the skill of focussing on information about the new language while reducing interference from the languages they already know.
column2: 这一优势可能源于这样一种本领：把注意力放在与新语言有关的信息上，同时减少已掌握的语言造成的干扰。

column1: Research also indicates that bilingual experience may help to keep the cognitive mechanisms sharp by recruiting alternate brain networks to compensate for those that become damaged during aging.
column2: 研究还表明，双语经验可能有助于认知机制保持敏锐：大脑会调动其他神经网络，补偿在衰老过程中受损的神经网络。
column7: alternate brain networks|其他可替代的脑网络

column1: Older bilinguals enjoy improved memory relative to monolingual people, which can lead to real-world health benefits.
column2: 与单语者相比，年长双语者的记忆力较好，这可能给他们的实际健康状况带来益处。

column1: In a study of over 200 patients with Alzheimer’s disease, a degenerative brain disease, bilingual patients reported showing initial symptoms of the disease an average of five years later than monolingual patients.
column2: 一项研究考察了200多名阿尔茨海默病患者。阿尔茨海默病是一种脑部退行性疾病。据患者报告，双语者出现最初症状的时间平均比单语者晚五年。
column4: degenerative brain disease|脑部退行性疾病

column1: In a follow-up study, researchers compared the brains of bilingual and monolingual patients matched on the severity of Alzheimer’s symptoms.
column2: 在后续研究中，研究者将阿尔茨海默病症状严重程度相当的双语患者和单语患者配对，比较他们的大脑。

column1: Surprisingly, the bilinguals’ brains had more physical signs of disease than their monolingual counterparts, even though their outward behaviour and abilities were the same.
column2: 出人意料的是，尽管两组患者的外在行为和能力相同，双语者脑内的病变迹象却比相应的单语者更多。
column3: physical signs of disease|疾病造成的实质性病变迹象

column1: If the brain is an engine, bilingualism may help it to go farther on the same amount of fuel.
column2: 如果把大脑比作发动机，那么双语能力可能让它在消耗相同燃料的情况下跑得更远。
column6: the same amount of fuel|同等数量的燃料

column1: Furthermore, the benefits associated with bilingual experience seem to start very early.
column2: 此外，双语经验带来的益处似乎从很早就开始显现。

column1: In one study, researchers taught seven-month-old babies growing up in monolingual or bilingual homes that when they heard a tinkling sound, a puppet appeared on one side of a screen.
column2: 在一项研究中，研究者训练了在单语或双语家庭中长大的七个月大婴儿，让他们学会一条规律：每当听到叮当声，屏幕的一侧就会出现一个木偶。
column7: one side of a screen|屏幕的一侧

column1: Halfway through the study, the puppet began appearing on the opposite side of the screen.
column2: 研究进行到一半时，木偶开始出现在屏幕的另一侧。

column1: In order to get a reward, the infants had to adjust the rule they’d learned; only the bilingual babies were able to successfully learn the new rule.
column2: 为了获得奖励，婴儿必须调整此前学到的规律。只有双语家庭的婴儿成功学会了新规律。

column1: This suggests that for very young children, as well as for older people, navigating a multilingual environment imparts advantages that transfer far beyond language.
column2: 这表明，对年幼的孩子和老年人来说，应对多语言环境所带来的优势，都能延伸到远远超出语言本身的领域。
column7: transfer far beyond|延伸到远超……的领域
